label: Inputs 2/k/r/b/p/l/z or <DEL> (encoding phase) in sequences starting with x/1/e/c/y/v/q/n/t
explanation: Candidate-positive unit driven by two things together: the current input token and the first original token. It fires mostly during the original phase and at <DEL> (87% of mass); copy-phase activity is weak. The input tokens that drive it are 2 (3.8x lift), then k, r, b, p, l, z, and <DEL>; g/h/t/i rarely drive it. It also needs the sequence to start with one of x, 1, e, c, y, v, q (about 2x lift each). Every top example starts with one of these and has a run of K-set tokens just before <DEL>. Activation is largest around t=2-3 and at <DEL>. The same first-token set shows up as out_tok in the weak copy-phase firings. It never fires at t=0, and it is weaker on repeated tokens (in_first=0 has 0.5x lift). The conjunction is still loose: precision is about 0.4 and about 40% of the mass falls outside it, so the hidden-state dependence is only partly captured.
